theory.intro: Some prisms have the same cross-section all the way through, but that cross-section is a **part of a circle** — a semicircle, a quadrant, or a sector. A semicircular gutter, a quarter-round moulding and a wedge of cheese are all like this. The prism rule $V = Ah$ still works: find the area $A$ of the curved cross-section, then multiply by the length $h$ the prism runs.
facts: **$V = Ah$**, where $A$ is the area of the curved cross-section and $h$ is the length (perpendicular distance) through the prism.
Cross-section areas: semicircle $A = \frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}$, quadrant $A = \frac{1}{4}\pi r^{2}$, sector $A = \frac{\theta}{360} \times \pi r^{2}$.
A semicircle is the sector with $\theta = 180^{\circ}$ and a quadrant is the sector with $\theta = 90^{\circ}$.
The area formulas use the **radius**; when a diameter is given, halve it first.
Use the calculator value of $\pi$, keep the working exact and round only at the last line; a length in cm and an area in cm² give a volume in cm³.
steps: Find the area of the curved cross-section using the semicircle, quadrant or sector formula.
Multiply the cross-sectional area by the length of the prism.

foundation.solution_text:
The cross-section is a semicircle of radius $r = 4$ cm.
$A = \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 4^{2}$
$= 8\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$160\pi = 8\pi \times h$
$h = \frac{160\pi}{8\pi}$
$= 20\text{ cm}$

development.question_text: A semicircular gutter has a cross-section of diameter $0.6$ m and runs $4$ m along a roof. Using $1$ m³ $= 1000$ L, find the capacity of the gutter, in litres, correct to $1$ decimal place.
development.solution_text:
The cross-section is a semicircle of radius $r = 0.3$ m.
$A = \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 0.3^{2}$
$= 0.045\pi\text{ m}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 0.045\pi \times 4$
$= 0.18\pi$
$= 0.5654\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
Capacity $= 0.5654\ldots \times 1000$
$= 565.4866\ldots$
$\approx 565.5\text{ L}$

development.question_text: A quarter-round timber moulding has a quadrant cross-section of radius $4$ cm and is $30$ cm long. A builder needs $5$ identical pieces. Find the total volume of timber, in cm³, correct to $1$ decimal place.
A wedge of cheese is a prism whose cross-section is a sector of radius $8$ cm and angle $45^{\circ}$, and it is $5$ cm thick. Find its volume, in cm³, correct to $1$ decimal place.
A prism with a quadrant cross-section is $8$ cm long and has a volume of $72\pi$ cm³. Find the radius of the quadrant, in cm.

A prism has a semicircular cross-section of radius $6$ cm and length $10$ cm. Sam calculated the volume as $360\pi$ cm³ by using $\pi r^{2}$ for the cross-section. Explain the mistake, then give the correct volume in exact form, in terms of $\pi$.
development.solution_text:
Sam used the area of a **full** circle, $\pi r^{2}$, but the cross-section is a semicircle, which is only half of that, so the area must be $\frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}$.
$A = \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 6^{2}$
$= 18\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 18\pi \times 10$
$= 180\pi\text{ cm}^{3}$

development.question_text: Trough A has a semicircular cross-section of radius $4$ cm and is $10$ cm long. Trough B has a quadrant cross-section of radius $6$ cm and is $10$ cm long. Using volumes correct to $1$ decimal place, decide which holds more and by how many cm³.
development.solution_text:
Trough A: $A = \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 4^{2}$
$= 8\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = 8\pi \times 10$
$= 251.3274\ldots \approx 251.3\text{ cm}^{3}$
Trough B: $A = \frac{1}{4} \times \pi \times 6^{2}$
$= 9\pi\text{ cm}^{2}$
$V = 9\pi \times 10$
$= 282.7433\ldots \approx 282.7\text{ cm}^{3}$
$282.7 - 251.3 = 31.4$
Trough B holds more, by $31.4$ cm³.

mastery.question_text: A tunnel is a $20$ m long prism. Its inside cross-section is a semicircle of diameter $6$ m and its outside cross-section is a concentric semicircle of radius $4$ m, the shape of the concrete arch. Find the volume of concrete used, in m³, correct to $3$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
The concrete cross-section is the outer semicircle minus the inner semicircle. The inner radius is $r = 3$ m and the outer radius is $R = 4$ m.
$A = \frac{1}{2}\pi R^{2} - \frac{1}{2}\pi r^{2}$
$= \frac{1}{2}\pi (4^{2} - 3^{2})$
$= \frac{7}{2}\pi\text{ m}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= \frac{7}{2}\pi \times 20$
$= 70\pi$
$= 219.9114\ldots$
$\approx 219.911\text{ m}^{3}$

mastery.question_text: A prism with a sector cross-section of radius $6$ cm and length $10$ cm has a volume of $60\pi$ cm³. Find the angle of the sector, in degrees.

A semicircular water trough has a radius of $0.5$ m and is $4$ m long. Water flows in at $100$ litres per minute. Using $1$ m³ $= 1000$ L, find how long it takes to fill the trough, in minutes, correct to $1$ decimal place.
mastery.solution_text:
$A = \frac{1}{2} \times \pi \times 0.5^{2}$
$= 0.125\pi\text{ m}^{2}$
$V = Ah$
$= 0.125\pi \times 4$
$= 0.5\pi$
$= 1.5707\ldots\text{ m}^{3}$
Capacity $= 1.5707\ldots \times 1000$
$= 1570.7963\ldots\text{ L}$
Time $= \frac{1570.7963\ldots}{100}$
$= 15.7079\ldots$
$\approx 15.7\text{ minutes}$
